Hi, I'm Michael Ng

STEM · Leadership · Innovation · Creativity

I'm an incoming college freshman from Houston, Texas who loves building things. Whether I'm designing precision CAD models or rebuilding mountain bikes, I'm most alive when I'm learning how things work and making something better. I'm drawn to ambitious projects, especially the kind that let me learn along the way.

This portfolio should give you a glimpse of some things I've worked on both at school and in my free time. I would love to connect! Feel free to shoot me an email anytime.

02

Projects

Mountain Bike

Vitus Nucleus 275 VR — Full Build & Maintenance

Assembled from parts in 2021 and continuously maintained and upgraded ever since. Working on this bike over several years has developed real mechanical intuition, including machine shop skills, precise torque management, and the fine maintenance of moving components like suspension seals, bearings, and hydraulic brake systems. Every upgrade taught me something new about how engineering decisions ripple through a system.

  • Installed internally-routed dropper post
  • 3 drivetrain replacements: Box 4 → Microshift Advent 9-speed → Shimano Deore 11-speed
  • Hydraulic brake flush, bleed, and servicing
  • Air suspension service; repacked hub bearings
  • Drilled frame for full-length cable housing
  • Multiple grip and pedal swaps; regular maintenance throughout
  • Installed new rear tire
Bike Build

Mongoose Switchback — Complete Build & Maintenance

A complete mechanical assembly project that taught me the intricacies of drivetrain geometry, cable tension systems, and how small tolerances between components can make or break a ride. Sourcing compatible parts, fitting every component correctly, and dialing in the final build deepened my understanding of how mechanical systems interact and sparked a broader interest in engineering. I continue to handle all ongoing maintenance.

Engineering

Landfill Design

An engineering design challenge that introduced me to environmentally-minded thinking in large-scale civil systems. Designing containment layers, leachate drainage, and gas capture systems for a model landfill taught me how engineers must balance functionality, cost, and long-term environmental responsibility, a perspective I've carried into all my technical work since.

Sustainability

Paper Recycling

A hands-on materials engineering project that walked me through the full paper recycling process, from pulping and fiber reclamation to sheet formation and drying. The iterative nature of the project taught me prototyping fundamentals: test, fail, adjust, repeat. It also touched on product marketing and the broader case for sustainable engineering, showing how material choices have real environmental and commercial consequences.

04

Service

Second Mile Mission

50+ hours volunteering in food assistance operations. Each shift directly impacted dozens of families per week, providing them with enough food to last approximately two weeks at a time — a tangible, meaningful contribution to food security in the Sugar Land community.

Houston Food Bank

20+ hours helping package and distribute food at one of the nation's largest food banks. The food processed during each volunteer session went on to support hundreds of Houston families — a humbling reminder of the scale at which community organizations can create impact.

Ranger Camp Leader

A full-circle moment — having gone through orientation as a freshman myself, I returned as a leader guiding a group of 20 incoming students through orientation activities, campus tours, and community-building exercises, helping ease their transition into high school.

Den Chief — Pack 1800

Another full-circle experience. Having come up through the Cub Scout program myself, I returned as Den Chief to lead a den of around 8 kids aged 8–10 from 2022–2025. I taught rank requirements and elective awards, facilitated weekly activities, and worked to give younger Scouts the same positive experience I had at their age.
